source_text: In opposition, "female genital cutting" (FGC) is favored by anthropologists and select public health scholars for its descriptive neutrality, avoiding presuppositions of cultural inferiority and enabling empirical analysis of varied outcomes, much like terminology for male circumcision or female cosmetic genital surgeries. [11]
